title: Immunoglobulins A, M, and G
what: This blood test shows how much of the three main types of antibodies you have. They protect you from infections.
why: For frequent or severe infections, when an immune problem is suspected, and for liver, blood, and joint conditions.
duration: the blood draw usually takes 5 minutes; results usually come in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: How often you get sick, and with what
If you had immunoglobulin or a blood transfusion
If you take steroids or drugs that suppress the immune system
If a child is being tested, their age. Normal values are different for children

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: It is usually better on an empty stomach or 4 hours after eating. Water is fine. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: Your health
prepare.text: If you have an acute infection now, ask your doctor if the test should be moved.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop anything on your own. Tell your doctor what you take.

steps: You sit down, and a band is tied above your elbow
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
Blood is taken from a vein into a tube
The band is removed, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse, and they will help you lie down
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes
Results usually come in 1 to 3 days
The doctor will read the result based on your age and health conditions

faq.a: Not always. Drops can be temporary. The doctor makes a diagnosis from the tests and how you get sick.
No. If they really are low, your doctor will choose treatment.

reminders.text: Immunoglobulin test tomorrow. Better on an empty stomach. Water is fine.
